75:1: The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as I swear la separated from I swear, except for Al-Hasan and Al-A’raj, as it was reported from them that they used to recite it as I swear by the Day of Resurrection, meaning: I swear by the Day of Resurrection, then the lam of the oath was added to it. The reading that I do not permit other than it in this position is la separated, I swear as a beginning, according to what the readers of the regions do, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers on it. Those who read it in the way we chose to read it differed in its interpretation. Some of them said that no is a connection, but rather the meaning of the statement is: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Yanaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, I swear by the Day of Resurrection. He said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: I do not swear. He said: I swear. Others said: Rather, la was used to emphasize the statement. Who said that? I heard Abu Hisham Al-Rifai say: I heard Abu Bakr bin Ayyash say: His saying I do not swear is an emphasis on the oath, like his saying No, by God. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: No is a rejection of previous words from the words of the polytheists who denied Paradise and Hell. Then the oath was started, and it was said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. He used to say: Every oath before it is a rejection of words, so it is necessary to place no before it, in order to differentiate between the oath that is denial and the oath that is renewed. He said: Do you not see that you say, starting with: By God, the Messenger is true, and if you say: No, by God, the Messenger is true, then it is as if you have accused people of lying who denied him. They also differed on this, whether it is an oath or not. Some of them said: It is an oath in which our Lord swears by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Abu al-Khair ibn Tamim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said to me: Where are you from? I said: From the people of Iraq. He said: Which of them? I said: From Banu Asad. He said: From their tribe of Harib, or from those upon whom God bestowed His blessings? I said: No, rather from those upon whom God bestowed His blessings. He said to me: Ask. I said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. He said: Your Lord swears by whomever He wills of His creation. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and I swear by the self-reproaching soul, he said: I swear by both of them. Others said: Rather, He swore by the Day of Resurrection, but He did not swear by the self-reproaching soul. He said: The meaning of His statement, And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul, is: I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said, He swore by the Day of Resurrection, but he did not swear by the self-reproaching soul. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: God swore by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul, and made la a response to the words that had preceded it from a people, and an answer to them. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings, because it is well-known from people’s speech in their conversations, when one of them says: No, by God, I will not do such-and-such, that he means without returning the speech, and by saying: By God, he is beginning an oath. The same is true of their saying: I swear by God that I will not do such-and-such. So if the well-known meaning of that is what we have described, then all that has come of similar examples should be in line with it, as long as nothing of it deviates from the well-known meaning that must be accepted. And after that: All of the evidence is in agreement that his saying, I swear by the Day of Resurrection, is an oath, so too is his saying, And I swear by the self-reproaching soul, unless an argument comes that indicates that one of them is an oath and the other is a predicate. We have shown that the reading of the one who reads the first letter of I swear by connecting the lām to I swear is an impermissible reading, because it contradicts what the argument is unanimously agreed upon. So the interpretation of the statement then is: No, the matter is not as you say, O people, that God does not resurrect His servants after their death. He swears by the Day of Resurrection. A group used to say: The resurrection of every soul is its death. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Mis`ar, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Alaqah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah ibn Shu`bah, who said: They say: The Resurrection, the Resurrection, but the Resurrection of one of them is his death. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Misa’ar and Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Qubays, who said: I attended a funeral in which Alqamah was present. When he was buried, he said: As for this man, his Resurrection has come.
75:2: And His saying: And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His saying the self-reproaching soul. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And I do not swear by the soul that blames itself for good and evil. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, And I swear by the self-reproaching soul, he said: It blames for good and evil. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul. He said: It blames for good and evil. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Abu al-Khair ibn Tamim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas, And I swear by the self-reproaching soul. He said: It is the self-reproaching soul. Others said: Rather, it means that she blames herself for what happened and regrets it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, with the self-reproaching soul, he said: It regrets what has passed and blames itself for it. Others said: Rather, the blameworthy one is the wicked one. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul: meaning the wicked one. Others said: Rather, it is the reprehensible one. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And I swear by the self-reproaching soul, he said: the blameworthy one. These sayings that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned them from, even if the wording of those who said them differed, are close in meaning. The most similar saying in that to the apparent meaning of the revelation is that it blames its speaker for good and evil, and regrets what has passed, and all the reciters agree on reading this by separating la from the word aqram.
75:3: And His statement: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? God Almighty says: Does the son of Adam think that We will not be able to assemble his bones after they have been scattered? Yes, even greater than that, that We will make his fingers, the toes of his hands and feet, and make them one thing like the hoof of a camel, or the hoof of a donkey. So he would not take what he ate except with his mouth like all other animals. But He separated the fingers of his hands to take with them, and to grasp and grasp if he wished and to stretch out, so His creation was good. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Abu al-Khair ibn Tamim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abbas said to me, and I said: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are able to proportion his fingertips. He said: If He had willed, He could have made him hoofed or barefoot.
75:4: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Yes, We are able to make his fingertips in perfect order, he said: I am able to make his hand a brazier like a camel’s hoof. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Yes, We are able to make his fingertips in perfect order. He said: We make him a hoof or a hoove. He said: It was narrated to us by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah, On the condition that we make his fingernails even. He said: On the condition that we make them like the hoof of a camel, or the hoof of a donkey. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Yes, We are able to proportion his fingertips, he said: He made it a hand, and made it fingers that He closes and spreads, and if He had willed, He could have gathered them together, so you protect yourself from the earth with your mouth, but He proportioned you with a beautiful creation. Abu Raja’ said: Ikrimah was asked, and he said: If He had willed, He could have made it like the hoof of a camel. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on the condition that we level his fingertips his feet, he said: like the camel’s hoof, so he does not do anything with them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Yes, We are able to make his fingertips in perfect order, God is able to make his fingertips like the hoof of an animal, or like the hoof of a camel, and if He had willed, He could have made them like that, for He only cleans His food with His mouth. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the condition that We make his fingertips even, he said: If He had willed, He could have made his fingertips like a camel’s hoof or the hoof of an animal. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, that We may make his fingertips in perfect order, he said: The fingertips are the fingers, meaning: We are able to make his structure like a camel’s hoof. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative of Qadir we are able. Some of them said: It is accusative because it is in the position of fa’ala we do, but when it is converted to fa’il we are able, it is accusative. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are able to put his fingers together. Then naqdir was converted to qadir we are able. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: It is accusative because of the exit from najma’ we gather, as if it was said in the statement: Does he think that We will not be able to dominate him? Yes, Qadir we are able to dominate more than you, meaning: Yes, We are able to do more than this. He said: People say Yes, we are able, but when it was converted to Qadir it is in the accusative case by mistake, because a verb is not accusative by changing it from fa’ala to fa’il. Don’t you see that you say: Ataqum ilaina doing so, but if you change it to fa’il you say: Aqiyam I am standing up, but it would have been a mistake to say Qaim standing up. He said: They used to cite the saying of Al-Farazdaq as evidence: I swear I will never curse anyone, whether a Muslim or an outsider, with false speech. They said: He only meant: I will not curse or go out. So when he diverted it to outside, he put it in the accusative case. He put it in the accusative case because he meant: I made a covenant with my Lord not to curse anyone, nor to go out from false speech. His saying: I will not curse, is in the accusative case. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is in the accusative case because we gather: that is, rather we gather it: that is, rather we gather it, able to level his fingers. This second statement is more likely to be correct according to the school of thought of the people of Arabic.
75:5: God Almighty says: The son of Adam does not ignore that his Lord is able to reassemble his bones, but he wants to continue ahead in disobeying God, nothing can stop him from doing so, and he never repents from it, and he postpones repentance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Abu al-Khair ibn Tamim al-Dhabi, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Rather, man desires to commit sin before him, he said: to go forward. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Rather, man desires to commit sin before him, meaning hope. Man says: I will work and then repent before the Day of Resurrection. And it is said: It is disbelief in the truth before the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, to carry out the ritual impurity in front of him, he said: to go ahead of him riding his head. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rather, man desires to commit sin before him, he said: Al-Hasan said: You will not find a son of Adam except that his soul is drawn to disobeying God step by step, except for the one whom God has protected. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, to commit sins before him, say: to commit sins before him. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi: Rather, man desires to commit adultery before him. He said: Forward. Abu Kurayb told us: He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah: Rather, man desires to commit immorality before him. He said: A footstep that does not depart from immorality. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, He will commit fornication in front of him. He said: I will repent. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that he is constantly pursuing the world and does not remember death. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Rather, man desires to commit sin before him, that it is hope. Man hopes: I will live and be afflicted with such and such of this world, and I will be afflicted with such and such, but he does not remember death. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Rather, the disbelieving person wants to deny the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Rather, man desires to commit sin before him, meaning: The disbeliever denies the reckoning. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Rather, man wants to commit sin before him, he said: He will deny what is before him on the Day of Resurrection and the reckoning. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Rather, man wants to disbelieve in the truth before the Resurrection. According to this statement, the ha in his saying before him is from the mention of the Resurrection. We mentioned the narration about that before.
75:6: His statement: He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ God Almighty says: The son of Adam, who is constantly disobeying God, asks: When is the Day of Resurrection? Procrastinating to repent. So God made that clear to him, saying: So when the sight is dazed, and the moon is eclipsed, and the sun and moon are joined together... the verse. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He is asked, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ He said, When is the Day of Resurrection? Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said, Whoever is asked about the Day of Resurrection, let him recite this Surah. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ When will that be? So he recited, And the sun and the moon will be joined together. He said: So that is how it will be on the Day of Resurrection.
75:7: And his saying: And when the sight flashes, the reciters differed in their recitation of that. Abu Ja`far al-Qari`, Nafi`, and Ibn Abi Ishaq recited it And when the sight flashes with a fat-ha on the ra`, meaning a person and a fat-ha at death. Shaybah, Abu `Amr, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as barq with a kasra on the ra`, meaning: frightened and split. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said: I asked Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ about it and he said: Barq with the kasra means hot. He said: I asked Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq about it and he said: Barq with the fatha. The barq of the thread, fire and lightning are only barq, and as for the sight, it is barq at death. He said: I informed Ibn Abi Ishaq of that and he said: I took my reading from the elders Nasr bin Asim and his companions, so I mentioned it to Abu Amr and he said: But I do not take from Nasr nor from his companions, so it is as if he was saying: I take from the people of Hijaz. The first of the two readings in this regard, in our opinion, is the correct one, with the kasra on the ra’, if it flashes, meaning: to frighten, split, and open from the horror of the Resurrection and the terror of death. This is how Arab poetry came about. Some narrators recited to me on the authority of Abu Ubaidah al-Kalabi: When Ibn Subaih came to me seeking it, I gave him Aisa from it, and he was delighted. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Zakariya al-Farra’ who said: Some Arabs recited to me: We suffer from a tender, blessed tenderness that drains dryness from the ten So, protect yourself and do not neglect me. Treat the wounds and do not be sad. With the opening of the letter ra, and he explained that he is saying: Do not be alarmed by the severity of the wound you have. He said: And thus the sight will shine on the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then when the sight is dazzled, he means by the dazzling of the sight: death, and the dazzling of the sight: is the Hour. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The sight flashed, he said: at death. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then when the sight is dazzled, means the sight is dazzled.
75:8: And his saying: And the moon was eclipsed means: The moon’s light was gone. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And the moon was eclipsed means its light was gone and it had no light. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan: And the moon was eclipsed means its light. He said: Its light was lost.
75:9: And His statement: And He gathered the sun and the moon, God Almighty says: And He gathered the sun and the moon in the blaze of light, so there is no light for either of them. And it is in the reading of Abdullah, as he mentioned to me, And He gathered the sun and the moon. And it was said: That they are gathered then rolled up, as God Almighty said, When the sun is rolled up (al-Takwir 81:1). And it was only said: And He gathered the sun and the moon because I mentioned that its meaning is He gathered them together. And some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: It was only said: And He gathered according to a doctrine and He gathered the two lights, as if it was said: And He gathered the two lights. And this is the statement of Al-Kisa’i. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the sun and the moon will be gathered together, he said: as balls on the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He gathered the sun and the moon, he said: He gathered them and threw them to the earth. And his saying, When the sun is rolled up, he said: Rolled up on the earth and the moon with it. He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abi Shaiba Al-Kufi, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, that he recited this verse one day: And He will gather the sun and the moon. He said: They will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, then they will be thrown into the sea, and it will be the Great Fire of God.
75:10: And his saying: On that Day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’ with the opening of the fa’, the readers of the regions read it that way, because the ‘ayn in the verb from it is broken, and if the ‘ayn from the verb is broken, then the Arabs open it in the source from it if they pronounce it on the form maf’al, so you say: fara yafru mufaran, meaning faraan, as the poet said: Ya Labakr, publish a video for me Ya Labakr, where, where is the escape? If this meaning is wanted from Maf’al, they say: Where is the escape, with the Fa open, and likewise Madab from Dab Yadub, as some of them said: As if the remains of the trace on his back were the bear’s pointed head, wandering. It may be chanted with a kasra on the dal, and the fatha is more common, and the Arabs may pronounce it that way, and it is a source with a kasra on the ayn, and Al-Farra’ claimed that they are two languages, and that he heard: He came on the torrent’s hump, and the torrent’s hump, and what is in his shirt is correct and correct, as for the Basrans, they open the ayn in the source of maf’al if the verb is on the pattern yaf’ul, and they only allow its kasra if what is meant by maf’al is the place to which one flees, and likewise the mudrab: the place in which one strikes if the ra’ is broken, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read that with a kasra on the fa’, and he said: The mafr is the place where an animal flees. The reading that I do not permit other than it is the fat-ha on the fa’ of mafar, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and that it is the well-known language among the Arabs when what is meant by it is fleeing, and in this case it means fleeing. The interpretation of the statement is: Man will say on the day he witnesses the horrors of the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Where is the escape from the horror of this that has descended, and there is no escape.
75:11: God Almighty says, No, there is no sin. God Almighty says: There is no escape that will benefit its owner, because his escape will not save him, nor will anything he can take refuge in, such as a fortress, mountain, or stronghold, from God’s command that has come, which is sin. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, No, there is no burden, meaning: no protection. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, No, no burden means: no fortress, no refuge. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibrahim bin Tarif told us, he said: I heard Mutraf bin Al-Shakheer reciting: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Then when he came to: No, no burden, he said: It is the mountain. When people flee, they say: Be upon you, burden. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Adham, who said: I heard Mutraf say: No, no burden. He said: No, no mountain. Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us: My father told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Qais, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: No, no burden. He said: No mountain. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, No, no burden, he said: The Arabs used to frighten each other. He said: Two men would be with their livestock, and they would not feel anything until the horses came to them, and one of them would say to his companion: O so-and-so, the burden, the burden, the mountain, the mountain. Abu Hafs Al-Hiri told me, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Abu Mawdud told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, No, no burden, he said: No mountain. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Mawdud, he said: I heard al-Hasan, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, No burden means no refuge and no mountain. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: No, no burden - no mountain, no protection, no place of escape. Al-Hasan said: When the Arabs in the pre-Islamic era feared an enemy, they would say: The burden is upon you, meaning the mountain is upon you. Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Abu Qilabah: No, no burden. He said: No fortress. Ahmad bin Hisham told us: Ubaidullah told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, the same. He said: Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said: Muslim bin Tahman told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, No burden, he said: No fortress. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: No burden means no mountain. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a client of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: No burden means no fortress. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Abu Hujair, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: There is no fortress. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: No, no burden meaning: the mountain in the language of Himyar. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, No, there is no blame, he said: There is no one who will be absent from that matter, no one who can escape from it.
75:12: And His statement: To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement. God Almighty says: To your Lord, O man, that Day is the final settlement, and He is the One who will establish all of His creation in their final settlement. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement, he said: The people of Paradise will settle in Paradise, and the people of Hell will settle in Hell. And he recited the statement of God, And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, if they only knew. (al-Ankabut 29:64) Others said: He meant by that the final destination is your Lord. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination: meaning the end.
75:13: God Almighty says: On that Day, man will be informed, the Day when the sun and the moon will be gathered together, and they will be judged by what he sent forward and what he left behind. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement, for what he sent forth and what he left behind. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: for what he sent forth of good or evil deeds before him, of what he did in this world before his death, and what he left behind after his death of bad and good deeds, or bad deeds that he will do after him. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind, meaning: what he did before his death, and what he established and acted upon after his death. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: For what he has sent forward of his deeds, and what he has left behind of the Sunnah that those who come after him have followed, whether good or evil. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: A person will be informed of the sin he committed and the obedience he will do. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind, meaning: of what he sent forth of disobedience and what he left behind of obedience, so he will be informed of that. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He will inform you of the beginning and end of his work. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind. He said: The first and last of his deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, the same. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is because of what he has presented of obedience and what he has left behind of the rights of God that he has neglected. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth of obedience to God, and what he left behind of what he wasted of the right of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: For what he has sent forward and left behind. He said: For what he has sent forward of his obedience and left behind of the rights of God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: what he has done of good or evil, and what he has left behind of what he has left behind in obedience to God. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind, he said: What he left behind is what he left behind of deeds that he did not do, what he left behind of obedience to God that he did not do, and what he sent forward is what he did of good or evil. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that it is report from God that a person will be informed of everything that he has done, good or evil, in his life, and what he has left behind of good or bad deeds that he has done and left behind. Likewise, what he has done, good or evil, has been done before, and what he has left behind of deeds that he was guilty of, but he did not do them, from what he has done and left behind. God has not specified some of that over others, so all of that is what a person will be informed of on the Day of Resurrection.
75:14: And His statement: Rather, man is a witness against himself. God Almighty says: Rather, man has observers over himself, from himself, who watch him with his actions and bear witness against him with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Rather, man is a witness against himself, meaning: his hearing, his sight, his hands, his feet, and his limbs. And the witness, according to this interpretation, is what Ibn Abbas mentioned of the limbs of the son of Adam, and it is raised by his statement, against himself, and man is raised by the pronoun that is mentioned in his statement, himself. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Rather, man is a witness against himself alone. Whoever says this statement has made insight a report for man, and has elevated man with it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Rather, man is a witness against himself. He says: Man is a witness against himself alone. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rather, man is a witness against himself, he said: He witnesses over his own actions. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Rather, man is a witness against himself, if you wish, by God, you will see him seeing the faults and sins of people, and the faults and sins of people, and heedless of his own sins. He said: And it was said: It is written in the Gospel: O son of Adam, you see the speck in your brother’s eye, but you do not see the log that is across from you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Rather, man is a witness against himself, he said: A witness against himself, and he read, “Read your record. Sufficient is yourself today as a reckoner against you.” (al-Isra’ 17:14), and whoever says this statement says: The ha’ was inserted in His statement, insight, and it is a predicate for man, just as it is said to a man: You are an argument against yourself, and this is the statement of some of the grammarians of Basra, and some of them used to say: This ha’ was inserted in insight, and it is an attribute of the male, just as it was inserted in narration and sign.
75:15: And his saying: Even if he presents his excuses, the narrators differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is that a person has witnesses against himself, even if he apologizes verbally for the sins he has committed, the transgressions he has committed, and the falsehood he has argued. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And if he were to present his excuses, meaning his apologies. Haven’t you heard that he said, Their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers (Ghafir 40:52), and God said, “And they will submit to God on that Day in peace, and we had not done any evil,” and their saying, By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists (al-An’am 6:23). Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, Rather, man is a witness against himself, he said: He is a witness against himself, even if he apologizes. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, He has insight into himself, even if he presents his excuses, even if he argues about it, he has insight into it. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Imran ibn Hudayr, he said: I asked Ikrimah, about his statement: Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he were to present his excuses. He said: So he was silent, so I said to him: Al-Hasan says: O son of Adam, your deeds are more important to you. He said: He spoke the truth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And if he were to present his excuses, he said: Their excuses that they will make on the Day of Resurrection, but they will not benefit from them. He said: The day when they will not be given permission to make excuses, and the day when they will be given permission, they will make excuses, but they will not benefit from them, and they will make excuses with lies. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Rather, man has insight into himself, even if he is detached. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told me: My father told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Qais, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zarara bin Awfa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And if he were to present his excuses, he said: If he were to be stripped of his sins. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Even if he lowered the curtains and closed the doors. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told me: Rawad told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, Even if he were to present his excuses, even if he were to lower the curtains and close the doors. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is even if he presents his excuses, they will not be accepted. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali told us: My father told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Qais, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And if he presents his excuses, his excuses will not be accepted. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Even if he presents his excuses, he said: Even if he apologizes. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: Even if he apologizes, because that is the most similar meaning to the apparent meaning of the revelation, and that is because God, the Most High, the Most Praised, informed us about man that he has a witness against him from within himself, in His saying: Rather, man is a witness against himself. So it was more appropriate to follow that, even if he argued on his behalf falsely and apologized without the truth, so his own testimony against him is more valid and more appropriate than his false apology.
75:16: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not move your tongue while reciting the Qur’an to hasten it. The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which he was told, Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten it. Some of them said: He was told that because whenever something from Him was revealed to him, he would hasten it, wanting to protect it out of his love for it. So he was told: Do not hasten it, for We will protect it for you. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would hasten to memorize it. God Almighty said: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” Ibn Abbas said: Like this, and he moved his lips. Ubayd ibn Ismail al-Hibari and Yunus told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, that when the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would hasten to memorize it. Yunus said: He would move his lips to memorize it, so God revealed: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” Ubaid bin Ismail Al-Habbari told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Aisha, who heard Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly, and he said: Do not move your tongue with it. He said: Like this, and Sufyan moved his mouth. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, he said: Whenever Gabriel came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with revelation, he would move his tongue and lips with it, and it would be difficult for him, and that was known in him. Then God revealed this verse regarding I swear by the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:“Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would move his lips, and that would be known. Saeed imitated him and said, Do not move your tongue to hasten it. He said, To hasten its memorization. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, who said: I heard Sa`id ibn Jubayr say: Do not move your tongue to hasten it. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, would come down with the Qur’an and move his tongue to hasten it. So he said: Do not move your tongue to hasten it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Rabi’i bin Aliyah told us: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding this verse: Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten it. He said: Whenever the revelation came down to him, he would hasten to speak it out of his love for it, so the verse was revealed: “Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, he said: Do not speak about that which We have revealed to you until We have completed its revelation to you. Then, when We have completed its revelation to you, then speak about it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Do not move your tongue with it, that he said: Whenever the revelation of the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would move his tongue with it for fear that he would forget it. Others said: Rather, the reason for which he was told that was that he used to recite the Qur’an frequently for fear of forgetting it, so it was said to him: Move your tongue to hasten it. It is up to us to collect it for you and recite it to you so that you do not forget. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, he said: He would not stop reciting the Qur’an for fear that he would forget it, so God said, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, it is upon Us to collect it for you, and recite it: that We recite it to you so that you do not forget. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Do not move your tongue with it, he said: He used to memorize the Qur’an for fear of forgetting, so he said to him: We have taken care of that for you, O Muhammad. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would remember it, so God said, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, We will preserve it for you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to move his tongue with it for fear of forgetting, so God revealed what you hear. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Do not move your tongue with it. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Qur’an frequently for fear that he would forget. The more similar of the two statements to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is the statement mentioned on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. That is because his statement, Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation, indicates that he was only forbidden from moving the tongue after hastening to do so before collecting it. And it is known that studying it for the purpose of remembrance was only done by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after God had collected for him what he was studying of that.
75:17: And His statement: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation, God Almighty says: Indeed, upon Us is the collection of this Qur’an in your chest, O Muhammad, until We establish it in it. And its recitation, He says: And its recitation until you recite it after We have collected it in your chest. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, it is upon Us to collect it He said: In your chest and to recite it He said: You recite it afterward. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, it is upon Us to collect it and to recite it means that We collect it for you, and to recite it means that We recite it to you so that you do not forget. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation, meaning: It is upon Us to collect it for you so that We may establish it in your heart. Others interpreted his statement, and His Qur’an, and its composition, as if the meaning of the statement to them was that it is up to us to collect it in your heart so that you may memorize it and compose it. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation, meaning its preservation and compilation. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He collected it and recited it. He said: He memorized it and composed it. It seems that Qatada directed the meaning of the Qur’an to the fact that it is a source from the saying of the speaker: This she-camel has read in her belly a fetus, if her womb has gathered a child, as Amr ibn Kulthum said: My arms are broken, blood-red, my brown-skinned, my camel has never read a fetus Meaning by saying: You have not read: You have not given birth to a child. As for Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak, they explained that to the fact that it is a source of the saying of the speaker: I read, I read the Qur’an and reading.
75:18: And His saying: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: So when We have sent it down to you, then listen to its recitation. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Ibn Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So when We have recited it means: So when We have revealed it to you, “then follow its recitation,” meaning: then listen to its recitation. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation means: So when We have revealed it to you, then listen to it. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If it is recited to you, then follow the laws and rulings contained therein. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. He said: When it is recited to you, then follow what is in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. He said: Follow what it has permitted and avoid what it has forbidden. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. He said: Follow what it has permitted and avoid what it has forbidden. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then follow his Qur’an, meaning: follow what is in it. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: If we explain it, then act upon it. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation, meaning: act upon it. The most correct of these sayings is the one who said: So when it is recited to you, then act upon it of commands and prohibitions, and follow what you are commanded to do in it, because it was said to him, Indeed, upon Us is its collection in your chest and its recitation. We have shown that the meaning of his saying, and its recitation is: and its recitation. This was explained by the meaning of his saying, “So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification,” God Almighty says: Then upon Us is the clarification of what is in it of what is lawful and unlawful, and its rulings are detailed for you. The interpreters differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.
75:19: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then it is for Us to make it clear, meaning its lawful and unlawful, so that is its clear explanation. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then it is for Us to make it clear, making clear what is permissible, avoiding what is forbidden, disobeying it, and obeying it. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Then it is up to us to explain it with your tongue. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then it is up to Us to make it clear. He said: Make it clear with your tongue.
75:20: God Almighty says to His servants addressed by this Qur’an, who prefer the adornments of this worldly life over the Hereafter: The matter is not as you say, O people, that you will not be resurrected after your death, nor will you be rewarded for your deeds. Rather, what has led you to say this is your love of this immediate world, and your preference of its desires over the Hereafter and its pleasures. So you believe in the immediate life and deny the hereafter. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, No! Rather, you love the immediate * and neglect the Hereafter. Most people choose the immediate, except for those whom God has mercy on and protected.
75:21: God Almighty says: And you abandon the Hereafter.
75:22: And His statement: On that Day some faces will be radiant. God Almighty says: On that Day some faces, meaning the Day of Resurrection, will be radiant: meaning beautiful and handsome from bliss. It is said from that: So-and-so’s face is radiant: if it is made beautiful from bliss. And God made his face radiant: if He made it beautiful like that. The interpreters differed on this, and some of them said what we said about it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari told me, he said: Adam told us, he said: Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Some faces that Day will be radiant. He said: Beautiful. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: On that Day some faces will be radiant. He said: The radiance of faces means their beauty. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, On that Day some faces will be radiant, he said: radiant means soft. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Some faces that Day will be radiant. He said: Beautiful faces. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Some faces that Day will be radiant. He said: From joy, bliss, and happiness. Others said: Rather, it means that she is happy. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, he said: Joyful, looking at their Lord. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: It means that she is looking at her Lord. Who said that? Muhammad bin Mansur al-Tusi and Ibrahim bin Saeed al-Jawhari told us: Ali bin al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us: al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Zayd al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: They will look at their Lord. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us: I heard my father say: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told me regarding His statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant from the bliss, looking at their Lord. He said: Yazid Al-Nahwi told me on the authority of Ikrimah, Ismail bin Abi Khalid, and elders from the people of Kufa, who said: Looking at their Lord. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari told us: Adam told us: Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, he said: Beautiful. Looking at their Lord, he said: Looking at the Creator, and it is right for them to be radiant while they are looking at the Creator. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam told me: Khalid bin Abdul-Rahman told us: Abu Urfajah told us, on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, regarding His statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: They will look at God, but their sight will not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is what He says, No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. (Al-An`am: 103) Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that she is waiting for the reward from her Lord. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: Waiting for reward from Him. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Looking to her Lord. He said: Waiting for the reward from her Lord. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Looking to her Lord, he said: Waiting for the reward. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Looking to her Lord. He said: She awaits the reward from her Lord, and none of His creation sees her. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant. He said: The radiance of bliss. “Looking to their Lord.” He said: Awaiting His provision and His grace. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Some people used to say about the hadith, They will see their Lord. So I said to Mujahid: Some people say that He sees. He said: He sees, but nothing sees Him. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, looking to her Lord, he said: She awaits from her Lord what she has. Abu Al-Khattab Al-Hassani told me, he said: Malik told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding His statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord, he said: Awaiting the reward. Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The lowest status of the people of Paradise is for the one who looks at his kingdom, his pleasures, and his servants, a distance of a thousand years, seeing its farthest point as he sees its lowest point. The highest status of the people of Paradise is for the one who looks at the face of God morning and evening. He said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Ashja’ told us, on the authority of Abu al-Sahba’ al-Mawsili, he said: The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who sees his couches, his servants, and his kingdom in a thousand years’ journey, so he sees its farthest point as he sees its nearest point. And the best of them in status is he who looks at the face of God morning and evening. The first of the two opinions on this matter, in our view, is the correct opinion that we mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah, that the meaning of this is that she looks at her Creator, and this is what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Abjar told me, he said: Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, he said: Isra`il bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of Ibn `Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who looks at his kingdom for two thousand years. He said: The best of them in status is he who looks at the face of God twice every day. He said: Then he recited: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: With whiteness and purity. He said: Looking at their Lord. He said: Looking every day at the face of God, the Almighty and Majestic.
75:23: God Almighty says: Looking to her Lord.
75:24: And His statement: And faces that Day will be gloomy, God Almighty says: Faces that Day will have changed colors, black and gloomy. It is said: I blackened a face, I blackened it with blackness: if you did that, and his face is black, so he is black between blackness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Basira, he said: Kashara. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And faces that Day will be gloomy meaning gloomy. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, frowning, he said: frowning. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Basira means: frowning.
75:25: And His statement: You think that He will do something terrible to her, God Almighty says: You know that He will do something terrible to her, and devastating means disaster. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, You think that He will do something terrible to her, he said: A disaster. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: She thinks that he will do something bad to her, meaning evil. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, You think that He will do something bad to her, he said: You think that she will enter Hell. He said: That is the bad report. The root of the word faqra is the brand that is applied to the nose.
75:26: God Almighty says: The matter is not as these polytheists think, that they will not be punished for their polytheism and disobedience to their Lord. Rather, when the soul of one of them reaches the collarbones at his death, he is astonished by it. Ibn Zayd said about God’s statement: No! When it reaches the collarbones. He said: The collarbone is itself.
75:27: Yunus told me this, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: “And it was said: Who will perform incantations?” God Almighty says: His family said: Who will perform incantations over him to cure him of what has befallen him? And they sought doctors and healers for him, but they did not avail him at all against the command of God that had befallen him. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his statement, Whoever performs an incantation, and some of them said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, “And it was said: ‘Who can recite incantations?’” He said: Is there an incantation that can recite incantations? Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Abu Qilabah: “And it was said: ‘Who can perform incantations?’” He said: Is there a doctor who can heal? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, the same. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Bastam, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding the statement of God Almighty: “And it was said: ‘Who has incantated?’” He said: He is the physician. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding And it was said that whoever performs an incantation he said: Is there a healer? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And it was said that whoever performed incantations means that they sought doctors for him, but they did not avail him at all against God’s decree. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And it was said, ‘Who has performed incantations?’ He said: Where are the doctors? And the incantations are those who perform incantations on him from death. Others said: Rather, this is from the words of the angels to one another, some of them saying to one another: Who will ascend with his soul? So he will ascend with it. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: No! When it reaches the collarbones, and it is said, ‘Who will ascend?’ He said: When it reaches his soul, it is ascended with, and the angels say, Who will ascend with it? The angels of mercy, or the angels of punishment? Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father, regarding His statement, And it was said, ‘Who can perform ruqyah?’ He said: It was reported to me on the authority of Abu Qilabah who said, Is there a doctor? He said: It was reported to me on the authority of Abu al-Juza’ that he said, The angels said to one another, ‘Who can perform ruqyah? The angels of mercy, or the angels of punishment?’
75:28: And His statement: And he thought it was separation, God Almighty says: And the one to whom this had befallen was certain that it was separation from the world, his family, his wealth, and his children. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And he thought it was the separation: meaning he was certain that it was the separation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And he thought it was the separation, he said: No one among God’s creation can prevent death, nor deny it, but he does not know whether he will die from that illness or from another, so the thought is as here.
75:29: And his saying: And the leg was entwined with the leg. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And the severity of the matter of this world was entwined with the severity of the matter of the Hereafter. Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg. He said: This world is hardship compared to the Hereafter. Ali told me, he said: Salih told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the leg shall be wound around the leg, meaning: The last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter, so hardship will meet hardship, except for whom God has mercy. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the leg will be entwined with the leg, meaning: And the world will be entwined with the hereafter, and that is the leg of the world and the hereafter. Have you not heard that He says, To your Lord, that Day, is the driving. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, he said: The matter of this world shall be entwined with the matter of the Hereafter at death. Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: And the leg will be entwined with the leg. He said: Al-Hasan said, the leg of this world with the hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Mujahid, who said: It is the matter of this world and the hereafter at death. Ali bin Al-Hussein told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, he said: The people of this world prepare the body, and the people of the Hereafter prepare the soul. Abu Hisham told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: Two things came together for him: the people prepared his body and the angels prepared his soul. Abu Hisham told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: The leg of this world is the leg of the Hereafter. Abu Hisham told us: Ja`far ibn `Aun told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, the same, and he added: It is said: Their wrapping up at death. Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah, who said: The world and the hereafter. He said: Ibn Yaman told us on the authority of Abdul Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of his father, who said: The matter of this world is based on the matter of the Hereafter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg. He said: The matter of this world is intertwined with the matter of the Hereafter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: He said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg. He said: Hardship with hardship, the leg of this world with the leg of the Hereafter. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us: I asked Ismail bin Abi Khalid, and he said: The deeds of this world are equal to the deeds of the Hereafter. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: They are this world and the hereafter. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, he said: The scholars say two opinions about it: Some of them say: The leg of the Hereafter is with the leg of this world, and others say: Say: No dead person dies except that one of his legs is entwined with the other. Ibn Zayd said: However, we do not doubt that it is the leg of the Hereafter. And he recited, To your Lord, that Day, is the driving. He said: When the Hereafter is entwined with the world, the driving will be to God. He said: And this is the opinion of most of those who say that. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the legs of the dead person were wrapped in the shroud. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Bashir bin Al-Muhajir told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And the leg was wrapped around the leg, he said: They wrapped them in the shroud. Abu Hisham told us: Waki’ and Ibn Al-Yaman told us, on the authority of Bishr Ibn Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: They are your legs when they are wrapped in a shroud. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the legs of the dead person are wrapped around each other at death. Who said that? Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of `Amir: And the leg was twisted around the leg. He said: The legs of the dead person. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Wahhab and Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, who said: His legs twisted when he was dying. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, the same. Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, something similar. Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik: And the leg is twisted around the leg. He said: At death. Abu Hisham told us: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: Your legs will be twisted at the time of death. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg: so that they may be bound by the command of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: The legs of the son of Adam are at death. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik: And the leg was wrapped around the leg. He said: They are his two legs when one of them was joined to the other. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the leg shall be wound around the leg. Qatada said: Have you not seen him when he strikes his other leg with his foot? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And his leg was twisted around his leg: his legs died and could not carry him to anything, for he was a burden on them. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, And the leg was twisted around the leg, he said: His legs at death. Others said: He meant that they would dry up at death. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik: And the leg will be twisted around the leg. He said: Their drying up at death. Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, the same. Others said: The meaning of this is: He followed one matter with another. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: Waki` told us: Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Isa: And the leg shall be twisted around the leg. He said: The command is for the command. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: And he followed one calamity with another. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: A calamity for a calamity. The first of the sayings that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: And the leg of this world was wrapped around the leg of the Hereafter, and that is the intensity of the distress of death with the intensity of the terror of the rising, and what indicates that this is its interpretation is His saying: To your Lord, that Day, is the driving. The Arabs say for every matter that is intense: He rolled up his leg, and uncovered his leg, and from that is the saying of the poet: If she rolls up her sleeves for you, bake her like a spring and never get tired What he meant by his saying the leg was twisted around the leg is that he stuck one of the two thighs to the other, as is said of a woman when one of her thighs sticks to the other: lafaa.
75:30: And His saying: To your Lord, that Day, is the drive. He says: To your Lord, O Muhammad, is the wrapping of the leg around the leg, the drive.
75:31: God Almighty says: He did not believe in the Book of God, nor did he pray to Him, but he denied the Book of God, and turned away and departed from obeying God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that?
