Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He neither believed nor prayed. He neither believed in the Book of God nor prayed to God.
75:32: God Almighty says: But he denied and turned away. He denied the Book of God and turned away from obeying God.
75:33: And His saying: Then he went to his family, swaggering. God Almighty says: Then he went to his family, turning back to them, swaggering in his gait. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He went to his family, swaggering. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiya bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Maysarah bin Ubaid, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, regarding his statement, Then he went to his family, swaggering, he said: swaggering. He said: This is the gait of the Banu Makhzum. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayyah, on the authority of Mujahid: He went to his family, swaggering. He said: He saw a man from Quraysh walking, so he said: This is how he used to walk, just as this one walks. He used to strut. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, stretching himself out, he said: strutted, and he was Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, that was his gait. It was said: This verse was revealed about Abu Jahl. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, stretching out, Abu Jahl said. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He neither believed nor prayed, but he lied and turned away, then he went to his family, swaggering, he said: This is about Abu Jahl, swaggering. What he meant by his saying stretches out is that he twists his back in a swaggering manner. The back is the swaying back, and from this is the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: When my nation walks in a swaggering manner, meaning that a man throws his hands and sways.
75:34: And His saying: It is better for you, then better, then better for you, then better. This is a warning from God upon a warning to Abu Jahl. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It is better for you, then better, then better, then better. Threat upon threat, as you hear. He claimed that this was revealed about the enemy of God, Abu Jahl. He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the hem of his garment and said: It is better for you, then better, then better, then better. The enemy of God, Abu Jahl, said: “Is Muhammad threatening me? By God, neither you nor your Lord can do anything to me. By God, I am more powerful than someone who walks between two mountains.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his hand - meaning Abu Jahl’s hand - and said: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting for you, then more fitting. He said: “O Muhammad, you and your Lord cannot do anything. I am more powerful than someone who walks between two mountains.” Then, on the day of Badr, he looked down upon them and said: God will not be worshipped after this day. God struck his neck and killed him in the worst way. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting, he said: Abu Jahl said: Muhammad threatens me, and I am the most honored of the people of Mecca and the valley. And he recited: “So let him call his assembly. We will call the guards of Hell. No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.” (al-Alaq 96:18) Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, who said: I said to Saeed ibn Jubayr: Was it something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said of his own accord, or was it something that God commanded him to do? He said: Rather, he said it of his own accord, then God revealed: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting for you, then more fitting.
75:35: God Almighty said: Then it is better for you, and better.
75:36: And His statement: Does man think that he will be left neglected? God Almighty says: Does this disbelieving man think that he will be left neglected, that he will not be commanded or forbidden, or that he will not worship God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Does man think that he will be left neglected? He said: neglected. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Does man think that he will be left neglected? He said: He is neither commanded nor forbidden. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Does man think that he will be left neglected? He said: The neglected is the one who is not required to do work and does not work.
75:37: God Almighty says: Was this not a thing that God could have done to revive him after his death, and to create him after his annihilation? Nutfah means: a little water in the man’s loins from semen. The reciters differed in their recitation of the word Yumna. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it as tamanna with a ta meaning: he wished for sperm. Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra recited it as Yumna with a ya meaning: the right hand of semen. The correct thing to say is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
75:38: And His statement: Then he was a clot, God Almighty says: Then he was blood after he was a sperm-drop, then a clot, then He proportioned him into a human being, speaking, hearing, and seeing.
75:39: God Almighty says: Then He made from him two mates, the male and the female. God Almighty says: Then He made from this human being, after He had proportioned him, a well-proportioned creation, children for him, males and females.
75:40: God Almighty says: Is He not able to bring the dead to life? God Almighty says: Is not He who did that, creating this human being from a sperm-drop, then a clot, until He made him a human being with male and female children, able to bring the dead to life from their death, and bring them into existence as they were before their death? He says: It is known that He who was able to create the human being from a sperm-drop of ejaculated semen, until He made him a normal human being, is not unable to bring a dead person to life after his death. And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would read that, he would say: Yes. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Is He not able to bring the dead to life? He mentioned to us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, he would say: Glory be to You, and yes.
